Cross-encoder reranking compares a query with each retrieved passage and produces a relevance
score. It is applied after candidate retrieval because pairwise inference is more expensive than
embedding search. The Hybrid RAG Service retrieves arXiv chunks with dense and lexical signals,
fuses them with reciprocal-rank fusion, and sends the leading candidates to a self-hosted CPU
cross-encoder. The reranker evaluates the whole query-passage pair, so it can distinguish lexical
overlap from whether a passage actually answers the question. Results are returned in descending
sigmoid score order, with original request index as a deterministic tie-break. The service bounds
each request to one hundred passages and truncates every pair to five hundred and twelve model
tokens. This fixture is repeated by the latency probe to approximate a four-hundred-token passage.
